title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling
main_claim: P3|prec,p_j=1|Cmax is solvable in deterministic polynomial time, O((L+2)^150020). The algorithm is a DP over all subsets of J described by Boolean formulas with at most 10000 leaves, built from rank thresholds and triple/cone membership tests in both frames. Its completeness rests on a structure theorem: every feasible full schedule has a recursive decomposition (center plus shared-cutoff separator walks on each side) in which every node set has a global description of fewer than 500 leaves, and every marked split has a relative description of that size.
coverage:
I read every proof in paper.tex, separators.tex, construction.tex, lists.tex, boundary.tex and descriptions.tex. Checked by hand:
- DP soundness (partition and compatibility) and the hierarchy-to-DP completeness lemma.
- The exchange and lexicographic-prefix arguments in the shared-cutoff walk, including the promoted job lying before s and the later old-low exceptions.
- Edge labels; carry and prune key preservation; the update-label identities.
- Pairwise disjointness of injections and the capacity-3 count; local flattening; the 21-leaf bound in old-low.
- The two properties of G (both the covering step and the early-exclusion localization through D_{a_-}, center and endpoint separators).
- I2 propagation through the first advance off the exterior boundary via the parent's I3 exchange, and I3 propagation in both the a'>a and a'=a cases.
- The global high/low child formulas, the relative split formulas with reversal, the leaf counts, and the B^5 N^13 running-time accounting.
I also wrote a brute-force simulation of the whole construction: lex-min normalization, center via Cor 3.4, walks, carry/injection/switch lists, G built through the paper's own flattened H_-^*, and pruning. At every child it asserts the separator properties, I1, I2, I3 (over up to 30 feasible reorderings of the child), the agreement of the S~ cutoff predicate with the edge cutoff, the qualifier and key-order identities, list length ≤ 5, both global child formulas, and both relative split formulas. It ran on about 5,500 nodes: 680 random and layered DAG instances with up to 22 jobs, depth up to 6, and about 2,700 direction switches. There were 0 assertion failures. Limitation: no simulated list ever had more than 2 entries, so the 3-injection/5-entry regime was verified only by hand, as were the leaf-count bounds. A further run (instances 400-479, up to 24 jobs) was stopped before it finished and is not counted.
sibling_notes: The family 124 board had no prior entries when I checked, so no companion results were used.
